newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: CHAMPALIMAUD GROUP SHARES SURGE IN PORTUGAL.
newsitem.headline: CHAMPALIMAUD GROUP SHARES SURGE IN PORTUGAL.

text.p: Shares in banks of the Antonio Champalimaud group surged on Lisbon bourse today, mainly because the market had revised higher its expectations for the results of flagship Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor.

BPSM rose more than 10 percent today to 2,540 escudos after analysts said they had raised forecasts for the bank's 1997 and 1998 results. The bank last week reported a 194 percent increase in first half profit to 8.4 billion escudos. Analysts said the target for BPSM shares by the end of 1997 was 3,000 escudos.

Champalimaud, Portugal's richest man, owns BPSM as well as Mundial Confianca, Banco Totta e Acores and Credito Predial Portugues, which all surged on Lisbon bourse today amid rosy prospects for the banking sector.
Mundial Confiance rose more than three percent to a high of 3,270 escudos and BTA rose more than four percent to a high of 3,714 escudos.

"The estimates of the market for BPSM's results in 1997 and 1998 were revised higher. I think this is one of the reasons for the strong rise in the stock," said one analyst, who forecast that BPSM would post a 1997 profit of 17.4 billion escudos, up from a previous forecast of 15.5 billion.
"The rise of BPSM is pulling along Mundial Confianca," he added. He said the continuing strength in BTA may be due to expectations that it will improve its results.

Another analyst said: "I felt that BPSM was worth 2,500 escudos, but now that this psychological barrier has been broken, anything can happen. BPSM is the star of the Champalimaud group, and Mundial Confianca is benefiting from this."

Another analyst, who expected that BPSM would post a 1997 profit of 18.3 billion escudos, said: "BPSM has room to rise this year to 3,000 escudos if its policy of provisions for its pension fund does not change in the second half."
BPSM posted a 1996 profit of about 12 billion escudos.
